answer: Karst-path lease with mirror probes: each agent leases a unique network inlet and a sparse checkpoint path through a karst-like state graph. Every epoch it submits HMAC(secret, checkpoint) plus a timing nonce from that inlet. If an identity is cloned, both copies emit identical mirror HMACs for the same checkpoint while appearing at different inlets; the collision flags the pair. Attacker cost: independent secret, distinct inlet, and separate checkpoint scheduling per sybil, plus cloning leaks.
